summary: Registers a media type for Open eBook Publication Structure package files. This memo is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: An OEBPS publication uses an OPF file to describe its contents. This RFC registers the media type software can use to identify that file.

questions: what is an opf package file
what media type identifies an opf file
subtitle: Registration of application/oebps-package+xml for OEBPS package files.

tldr.problem: Software needs a media type to identify OEBPS Package Files when they are edited, referenced, or transferred.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers application/oebps-package+xml for the XML file that describes an OEBPS publication and identifies its other files.
tldr.outcome: The registration specifies UTF-8 or UTF-16 XML encoding and the .opf file extension.

today: RFC 4839 is an Informational media type registration for OEBPS Package Files. The unit metadata lists no update or replacement.

sections.title: The OEBPS Package File
sections.content:
An Open eBook Publication Structure package file, or OPF file, is an XML file describing an OEBPS publication. It identifies the other files in the publication and provides descriptive information about them.

The RFC says a media type is needed to identify OPF files when edited on disk, referenced by OEBPS Container files, or used where media types are applied.
sections.plainLanguage: The OPF file describes the other parts of an OEBPS publication. Software needs a label that identifies this XML file.

sections.title: The Media Type Registration
sections.content:
IANA registered the media type application/oebps-package+xml. It has no required or optional parameters, and its encoding is UTF-8 or UTF-16 XML.

The registration lists .opf as the file extension and describes intended usage as COMMON. The OEBPS specification is maintained by the International Digital Publishing Forum.
sections.plainLanguage: The registered media type is application/oebps-package+xml, and .opf is its file extension. The file uses UTF-8 or UTF-16 XML.

sections.title: Processing OPF Files
sections.content:
The RFC notes that OPF files are well-formed XML but may be authored with malformed or malicious data. It advises processors to check the size and validity of retrieved data.

The OEBPS Package File format has no provision for encryption, signing, or authentication within the file itself.
sections.plainLanguage: Applications should check the data they read from OPF files. The format itself does not provide encryption, signing, or authentication.

references.text: "Open eBook Publication Structure 1.2", International Digital Publishing Forum (IDPF), New York, NY USA, 2002.
Freed, N. and J. Klensin, "Media Type Specifications and Registration Procedures", BCP 13, RFC 4288, December 2005.
